findings.title: Idle-timeout config accepts zero, negative and boolean values
findings.description: `get_typed_config(..., int)` only checks `isinstance(value, int)`. Because `bool` is a subclass of `int`, a TOML `true` passes for `pipeline.background_idle_timeout_s`. `_coerce_value` also accepts `0` or `-5` without a range check. The value goes straight into `asyncio.timeout(idle_s)` in `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py#_read_turn`. With `0` or a negative value the first wait after the dispatch's own result times out immediately. `_stop_background` then kills every background agent the moment the dispatch starts waiting. That silently defeats the wait-for-agents behavior this slice adds. The project's "fail explicitly" rule suggests rejecting non-positive values at `sq config set` and in the typed read. The bool branch is checked before int, so the guard can be added without disturbing it.

findings.title: Settings-source resolution is duplicated across two call sites
findings.description: `pipeline_setting_sources(include_user=get_typed_config("pipeline.user_settings", bool, cwd=...))` plus the `pipeline.auto_memory` read is written once in `one_shot_dispatch_with_telemetry` and again in `src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py#open_pipeline_session`. The two builders can drift apart. A single `resolve_pipeline_settings(cwd)` helper in `providers/sdk/settings.py` would keep the policy in one place. `test_settings_policy.py` guards against drift today, so this is not blocking.

findings.title: Pyright suppression at the SDK options boundary
findings.description: `SdkSettings.setting_sources` is `list[str]`, while the SDK expects a list of literals, so the call carries `# pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]`. Typing the field with the SDK's `SettingSource` literal would remove the suppression. `provider.py` has the same `# type: ignore[arg-type]` on `base_env=kwargs.get("env")`.

findings.title: Broad catch in `_stop_background` is justified and compliant
findings.description: The `except Exception  # noqa: BLE001` carries a comment explaining that the SDK raises a bare `Exception`. It logs with `logger.exception`, continues to the next task id, and is covered by `test_stop_task_failure_is_logged_and_next_id_still_stopped`. The reconnect failure path in `_reconnect` also logs and re-raises, and records `unusable_reason`. Both follow the project's exception-handling rules.

findings.title: Test coverage matches the new behavior
findings.description: Tests cover background ledger states, own-result detection, leftover injected turns, stream end with an agent still tracked, idle timeout, and subagent prose exclusion. They also cover the bool config round-trip, the settings policy for every automated SDK path, and reconnect failure at the compact, summary and batch levels. The scripted-client fixtures use real SDK message types, not loose mocks.

structured_findings.summary: Idle-timeout config accepts zero, negative and boolean values
Settings-source resolution is duplicated across two call sites
Pyright suppression at the SDK options boundary
Broad catch in `_stop_background` is justified and compliant
Test coverage matches the new behavior
